questions.stem: What is the main job of the linen room in a villa or hotel?
options: To store, issue, receive and keep track of clean linen
To cook the meals for the guests and the staff
To clean the guest rooms and the public areas
To keep the guests' luggage while they are out

questions.stem: Which of these is "bed linen"?
options: Bath mats and face cloths
Tablecloths and dinner napkins
Fitted sheets and pillowcases
Pool towels and beach towels

questions.stem: Which item is part of "table linen"?
options: A duvet cover
A napkin
A bath towel
A pillow protector

questions.stem: What does "one par" of linen mean?

The amount of linen sent to the laundry each month
A single sheet kept spare in each guest room
Enough linen to make up every room once

Open shelf, take what you like
Clean for dirty, item for item
Pay as you go

Count it out and record it on the issue sheet

Issue it only after the guests have checked out

questions.stem: Soiled linen arrives at the linen room. What should you do first?
options: Count and sort it by type, wearing gloves
Shake each item hard to get the dust out
Put it straight on the clean linen shelves
Leave it in a heap until the end of the week

questions.stem: Why should soiled linen never be shaken?
options: It makes the linen dry out much too quickly
It stretches the fabric and spoils its shape
It spreads germs, dust and lint into the air
It makes the linen harder to count correctly

questions.stem: Soiled linen from a room has blood on it. How should it be handled?
options: Rinse it in the guest's bathroom sink first
Mix it with the other linen so no one notices
Throw it away in the general rubbish bin
Wear gloves and bag it apart, as the policy says

questions.stem: What should you check for in soiled linen before it goes to the laundry?
options: The name of the guest who used each item
Whether the item still smells of the guest's perfume
Items left in it, such as needles or phones
Whether the colour has faded since last week

options: The trolley would be too heavy to push safely

questions.stem: Which is the best place to store clean linen?
options: On slatted shelves in a clean, dry, airy, locked room
On the floor of the laundry, near the washing machines
In a damp store room next to the cleaning chemicals
In plastic bags on the open veranda in the sunshine

So that it takes up less space in the room
So that it dries faster in the hot sun
To keep it clean, dry and free from pests

questions.stem: Clean linen has been put away while it was still damp. What problem may follow?

Black or grey spots and a musty smell
The colours will become brighter
It will be stiff and hard to fold

questions.stem: Where should newly laundered linen be placed on the shelf?
options: On top of the pile, so that it is used first
On the floor in front of the shelf
At the bottom or back of the pile
In a separate room that is never used

questions.stem: Why is linen stock rotated, so that the oldest clean linen is issued first?
options: So all linen wears evenly and lasts longer
So that the newest linen is always used first
So that guests can choose the colour they like
So that the linen room needs fewer shelves

options: So that the staff can take a longer break
So that the linen picks up the room's smell
So that the linen room looks fuller to visitors

Put it on the shelf with the other sheets

To tell guests how old their room's linen is

Once every five years, when the linen is replaced
At regular, set times, such as once a month
Never, because the issue sheets are enough

questions.stem: During a stock-take, where must linen be counted?
options: Only on the shelves in the linen room itself
Only in the guest rooms that are let that day
Only the linen that is in the laundry

questions.stem: While counting soiled linen, you find a guest's watch inside a pillowcase. What should you do?

options: Issue a clean one in the right size and record it

questions.stem: Why is the linen room kept locked when no one is working in it?

So guests cannot see how it is organised

To prevent theft and keep track of stock

questions.stem: Who should hold the key to the linen room?

Only the staff the supervisor names

Whoever arrives at work first each day

questions.stem: A room attendant needs more linen than her issue sheet shows. What should she do?

Take it from another attendant's trolley when she is away

questions.stem: Why does the linen room fold every item to the same standard?
options: So that the linen dries more quickly on the shelf
So that items stack neatly and count easily

So that the linen can be stored without being washed

questions.stem: How can you quickly tell a queen sheet from a king sheet in the linen room?
options: By smelling the sheet to find its size
By guessing from how heavy the pile is
By its size label or coloured hem stitching
By asking a guest which size they think it is

questions.stem: Many properties use poly-cotton sheets. What is poly-cotton?
options: A sheet made only of silk and wool
A sheet made of strong paper, for one use only
A cotton sheet with a plastic coating
A blend of polyester and cotton threads

questions.stem: A full bag of wet soiled towels is very heavy. How should you move it?
options: Drag it along the floor behind you by its drawstring
Use a trolley, or share the load, lifting safely
Throw it down the stairs to the laundry
Lift it quickly with a bent, twisting back

questions.stem: Which item of PPE should you wear when sorting soiled linen?
options: A pair of sunglasses
A woollen hat
Disposable gloves
Ear protectors

questions.stem: Why is smoking banned in and near the linen room?
options: Smoke makes the linen hard to fold neatly
It makes the linen room too warm for staff
Smoke changes the colour of the shelves
Linen burns easily, and fire can spread fast

questions.stem: A room attendant finds bed bugs on sheets from a guest room. What should happen to the linen?
options: Seal it in a bag, label it and report it at once
Shake it out on the balcony, then put it back
Put it on the clean shelf after a quick brush
Hide it at the bottom of the soiled linen pile

questions.stem: The linen room is next to the laundry chemicals store. What is the safe practice?
options: Keep chemicals on the same shelves as linen
Put open bottles on top of the folded linen
Keep chemicals apart from linen, closed and labelled
Pour chemicals into unlabelled bottles

questions.stem: The linen room is running short of bath towels. Who should you tell?
options: The guests, so that they use fewer of the towels
No one, as the laundry will sort it out
The gardener, who may have spare ones
Your supervisor, so the shortage can be fixed

questions.stem: What should you do after handling soiled linen and taking off your gloves?
options: Wash your hands well with soap and water
Wipe your hands on a clean towel from the shelf
Go straight to fold the clean linen
Put the used gloves back in the box

questions.stem: How should a room attendant's linen trolley be loaded?
options: Soiled linen on the top shelf, clean linen below
Clean on the shelves, soiled in a separate bag
All linen together in one big bag on the handle
As much as possible, piled above head height

questions.stem: Which is NOT a common cause of damage to linen?
options: Using linen as a rag to wipe up spills
Too much bleach in the wash
Storing linen on clean, slatted shelves

essays.stem: Describe the main duties of a linen room attendant during a normal working day.
essays.modelAnswer: The linen room attendant starts early, so that clean linen is ready before the room attendants begin. They unlock the linen room, check that it is clean and tidy, and set out the issue sheets. They issue clean linen to each room attendant against the soiled linen returned, item for item, and record it. During the day they receive soiled linen, wearing gloves, count and sort it by type, check it for items left inside, and bag it for the laundry, keeping it away from clean stock. When clean linen comes back, they count it against the laundry list, inspect it for stains, tears and wear, and put rejects aside for rewash, repair or discard. They fold to standard, store linen on the shelves with the newest at the bottom, issue uniforms, keep the records up to date, report shortages and lock the room at the end of the shift.
markingPoints: Prepares early: opens, checks the room and sets out issue sheets
Issues clean linen item for item and records it
Receives, counts, sorts and bags soiled linen safely with gloves
Counts and inspects returning clean linen; separates rejects
Folds and stores with rotation, issues uniforms, keeps records, reports shortages and locks up

essays.stem: Explain what "par stock" is and why a property keeps several par of linen. Use an example with numbers.
essays.modelAnswer: One par is the amount of linen needed to make up every room in the property once. For example, a villa with 5 bedrooms, each with 2 bath towels, needs 10 bath towels for one par. A property keeps several par because linen is in different places at the same time: one par is in the rooms being used, one par is in the laundry being washed, and one par is clean on the shelves ready to issue. Some properties also keep a further par in the store for emergencies, losses and replacement. So, with 3 par, the villa needs 3 × 10 = 30 bath towels. Keeping enough par means rooms can always be made up on time, linen gets time to rest between uses so it lasts longer, and the property is not caught short when the laundry is late or a lot of linen is condemned.
markingPoints: One par = enough to make up every room once
Correct worked example of one par
Linen is in rooms, in the laundry and on the shelves at the same time (and spare in store)
Correct calculation for several par
Benefits: rooms made up on time, linen lasts longer, cover for delays and losses

essays.stem: Describe the steps for issuing clean linen to room attendants and receiving soiled linen from them, and say what records are kept.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start of the shift, each room attendant brings the soiled linen from their rooms, already bagged and kept apart from clean linen. Wearing gloves, the linen room attendant counts the soiled items by type, such as sheets, pillowcases and towels, with the room attendant watching, and records the numbers on the linen exchange or issue sheet. The linen room attendant then issues the same number of clean items, item for item, plus any extra on a signed requisition from the supervisor. Both people sign the sheet. Clean linen goes on the room attendant's trolley shelves, and soiled linen goes in a separate bag or bin for the laundry. Any items with stains, tears or bed bugs are noted. At the end of the day, the totals on the issue sheets are checked against the stock, and any difference is reported to the supervisor.
markingPoints: Soiled linen arrives bagged and apart from clean
Counted by type with gloves, in front of the room attendant, and recorded
Clean linen issued item for item, extras only on a requisition
Both sign the issue or exchange sheet; clean and soiled kept separate
Totals checked at the end of the day and differences reported

essays.stem: Describe how clean linen should be stored, and explain the reasons for each point.
essays.modelAnswer: Clean linen is stored in a room that is clean, dry, cool and well aired, because damp causes mildew and smells, and heat dries out the fibres. Linen is kept on slatted shelves off the floor and away from the walls, so that air can move around it and it stays free of dust, damp and pests. It is kept out of direct sunlight, which fades and weakens fabric. Items are sorted by type and size, with labelled shelves, so that they are quick to find and count. Freshly laundered linen goes at the bottom or back of each pile, so that older stock is used first and all of it wears evenly. Chemicals, food and dirty items are never stored with clean linen. The room is kept locked when no one is working there, to stop theft, and no one smokes nearby because linen burns easily.
markingPoints: Clean, dry, cool, airy room (damp causes mildew)
Slatted shelves off the floor and away from walls (air, dust, pests); out of sunlight
Sorted and labelled by type and size
New linen at the bottom or back so older stock is used first
No chemicals or soiled items; locked; no smoking

essays.stem: Explain how to handle soiled and contaminated linen safely and hygienically.
essays.modelAnswer: Soiled linen can carry germs, so it is handled as little as possible. Staff wear disposable gloves and, where linen is very dirty, an apron. Linen is stripped from the bed carefully and never shaken, because shaking spreads germs, dust and lint. Before bagging, staff check for items left inside, such as needles, razors, jewellery or phones, by feeling carefully rather than putting a hand deep inside. Soiled linen goes straight into a bag or bin, never on the floor or on a guest's furniture, and it is carried apart from clean linen. Linen with blood, vomit or other body fluids is kept apart in a separate bag, such as a water-soluble bag where the property uses them, labelled and handled as the policy says. Wet linen is sent to the laundry quickly so that it does not go mouldy. Afterwards, staff remove gloves and wash their hands well.
markingPoints: Gloves (and apron where needed); handle as little as possible
Never shake; never put on the floor
Check carefully for sharps and items left inside
Separate bags; contaminated linen kept apart and labelled as the policy says
Clean and soiled kept apart; sent promptly; hands washed afterwards

essays.stem: Describe how you would inspect clean linen, and what you would do with items that are stained, torn or worn out.
essays.modelAnswer: As clean linen comes back from the laundry, I would check each item as I fold it, in good light, on a clean table. I would look for stains, marks, holes, tears, loose hems, frayed edges, thin areas, colour fading and any smell, and check that it is properly dry. Good items are folded to standard and stored. Items that are still stained are sent back to the laundry for stain treatment and a rewash. Items with small tears, holes or loose hems are sent to the sewing room or the seamstress for repair, if they are worth mending. Items that are too worn, thin or badly damaged to use are condemned: they are recorded on the discard record and, where the property allows, made into cleaning cloths or rags. Every reject is recorded, and the supervisor is told if many items fail, so that the cause can be found.
markingPoints: Checks each item in good light while folding
Looks for stains, tears, holes, loose hems, wear, fading, damp or smell
Stained items back to the laundry for treatment and rewash
Torn items to the sewing room for repair
Worn-out items condemned, recorded and reused as cloths; supervisor told of patterns

essays.stem: Describe how to carry out a linen stock-take.
essays.modelAnswer: A stock-take is done at set times, such as at the end of each month, at a quiet time agreed with the supervisor. First, the stock sheets are prepared with each item and size, such as king sheets, queen sheets, pillowcases, bath towels, pool towels and napkins. The linen is then counted everywhere it is kept: on the linen room shelves, in the floor stores, in the guest rooms that are made up, on trolleys, and at the laundry or outside laundry. Two people may count together to avoid mistakes. The numbers are written on the stock sheets, and the totals are compared with the last stock-take, the new linen bought and the items on the discard record. Any shortage that cannot be explained is reported. The supervisor uses the results to check that there is enough par stock and to order new linen in time.
markingPoints: Done at set, regular times, agreed with the supervisor
Stock sheets list each item and size
Counts everywhere: shelves, floor stores, rooms, trolleys, laundry
Totals compared with last count, purchases and discards
Shortages reported; results used to check par and order linen

essays.stem: Explain how to send linen to an outside laundry and check it when it comes back.
essays.modelAnswer: Before sending, I would sort the soiled linen by type and count it, wearing gloves. I would write each type and number on the laundry list in two copies, with the date, and note any special items, such as stained or contaminated linen in separate, labelled bags. The driver and I would both sign the list, and I would keep one copy. When the clean linen comes back, I would count each type against my copy of the list before the driver leaves, if possible, and check the quality: clean, dry, no stains or damage, and folded well. I would record any items missing or damaged, ask the driver to sign the note, and report it to my supervisor so that the laundry can be asked to find the items or pay for them. The lists are filed so that the office can check the laundry's bill.
markingPoints: Sorts and counts soiled linen with gloves before sending
Writes a dated laundry list in two copies, with special items noted
Both sign; a copy is kept
On return, counts against the list and checks quality
Records and reports shortages or damage; lists kept to check the bill

essays.stem: Describe the health and safety risks in a linen room and how each can be controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: Lifting heavy, wet bags of linen can hurt the back, so staff use trolleys, share loads and lift with bent knees and a straight back. Reaching high shelves can cause falls, so a proper step stool is used, never a chair or the shelves themselves. Germs on soiled linen can cause infection, so staff wear gloves, never shake linen, keep clean and soiled apart and wash their hands. Sharp items such as needles or razors may be hidden in linen, so staff check carefully and use a sharps box. Linen and lint burn easily, so smoking is banned, dryer lint is cleared, and fire exits and extinguishers are kept clear. Chemicals can harm skin and eyes, so they are stored apart, labelled and used with the right PPE, following the SDS. Wet floors and trailing bags cause slips and trips, so spills are wiped up and walkways kept clear.
markingPoints: Manual handling: trolleys, shared loads, safe lifting; step stool for high shelves
Infection: gloves, no shaking, separation, hand washing
Sharps hidden in linen: careful checks and a sharps box
Fire: no smoking, lint cleared, exits and extinguishers clear
Chemicals and slips: stored apart with PPE and SDS; spills cleared, walkways clear

essays.stem: Explain how the linen room keeps linen and uniforms secure, and how it controls losses.
essays.modelAnswer: The linen room is kept locked when no one is working in it, and only staff named by the supervisor hold the key. Linen is issued only on a clean-for-dirty basis, item for item, and any extra is given only on a signed requisition, so the numbers always match. Every issue, return and laundry delivery is counted and signed for. Uniforms are issued one clean for one soiled, in the right size, and recorded against each staff member's name, and they are returned when the staff member leaves the job. Condemned items are written on the discard record before they are cut up or thrown away, so that they are not counted as lost. Regular stock-takes show whether any items are missing. Shortages, damage or theft are reported to the supervisor at once, so that the cause can be found and stopped.
markingPoints: Room locked; only named staff hold keys
Clean-for-dirty issue; extras only on a signed requisition
Every movement counted and signed for, including the laundry
Uniforms issued and recorded by name, returned on leaving; discards recorded
Regular stock-takes; shortages and theft reported promptly

practical1.title: Linen stock-take, par check and shelf set-up
practical1.brief: The assessor sets up the Centre's linen store or a training room with mixed clean linen: sheets of two or three sizes, pillowcases, bath towels, hand towels, face cloths, bath mats, pool towels and napkins, some in the wrong places and a few rejects (marked stains, small tears, worn items). The assessor gives the number of rooms, the items each room needs and the number of par the property keeps. As a group, prepare a stock sheet, then each member counts one or two types of linen and records the numbers. Together, work out one par and the full par stock for each item, compare it with the count and list the shortages to order. Take out the rejects and record each one as rewash, repair or condemned. Then set up the shelves: sort by type and size, label each shelf, fold untidy items to standard, and place the stock so that older linen is issued first. Each member explains their part and their sums to the assessor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and sheets to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Mixed clean linen of several types and sizes, with a few marked rejects (from the assessor)
Shelving or tables, shelf labels, markers and tape
Stock sheets, a par worksheet, a reject and discard record, pens and a calculator
The room numbers and par figures (from the assessor)
A step stool for high shelves
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The linen store before the stock-take
Members counting their types of linen
The par worksheet with shortages worked out
The rejects separated and the reject and discard record filled in
Folded items showing the house standard
checklist: Counted their types of linen accurately and recorded them clearly
Worked out one par and the full par stock correctly
Found the shortages correctly and listed what to order
Picked out every reject and recorded it as rewash, repair or condemned
Sorted and labelled shelves by type and size, off the floor
Placed stock so that older linen is used first
Folded items neatly to the house standard
Lifted safely and used the step stool for high shelves
safety: Lift piles of linen with bent knees and a straight back; do not carry piles that block your view
Use the step stool for high shelves; never climb on shelves or chairs
Keep walkways clear of linen and boxes
Report any shelf that is loose or unsafe

practical2.title: Linen exchange, inspection and folding
practical2.brief: Set up the linen room counter with issue sheets, a stock of clean linen and separate bins for soiled linen. The assessor gives each group member a role card: linen room attendant or room attendant (members swap so that everyone does each role). Room attendants bring bags of "soiled" linen (practice linen tagged as soiled, or used linen from the Centre's training rooms). Wearing gloves, the linen room attendant counts the soiled items by type in front of the room attendant, checks for items left inside (the assessor hides a safe item such as a plastic spoon or a sock), records the count, and issues clean linen item for item. Both sign the issue sheet. Then, as a group, inspect a batch of clean linen from the "laundry", count it against the laundry list, separate rejects, and fold sheets, towels, pillowcases and napkins to the house standard. Finally, issue a uniform from the uniform rack and record it. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and sheets to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A counter or table, linen exchange or issue sheets, a laundry list, a uniform issue record and pens
Clean linen stock (sheets, pillowcases, towels, napkins)
Bags of practice "soiled" linen with safe hidden items (from the assessor)
Separate bins or bags for soiled linen and for rejects
A uniform rack with uniforms in several sizes
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The counter set up, with clean and soiled areas kept apart
Soiled linen being counted with gloves on
The item found inside the linen
The clean batch checked against the laundry list, with rejects set aside
Sheets, towels, pillowcases and napkins folded to standard
checklist: Wore gloves for soiled linen, did not shake it and washed hands afterwards
Checked soiled linen for items left inside, safely
Counted and recorded soiled linen by type correctly
Issued clean linen item for item, and both signed the sheet
Kept clean and soiled linen apart at all times
Counted the clean batch against the laundry list and recorded any difference
Folded each type of item neatly to the house standard
Issued a uniform in the right size and recorded it
safety: Wear gloves for soiled linen; never shake it; wash your hands afterwards
Feel bags carefully from the outside first; do not push your hand deep inside
Lift bags with bent knees and a straight back, and do not overfill them
Keep clean and soiled linen and their trolleys apart
